faq: Where do the tracking updates come from?
From the carrier through your store or tracking app. We check that the tracking number reaches the customer, and that status changes such as delivered are picked up correctly.
Do text messages need customer permission?
Yes. We set up opt-in wording that follows the rules for text messages, and we send only to those who agreed. We do not send marketing under a service message.
Can I send messages in other languages?
Yes, where your platform supports translated notifications. Tell us which languages you need, and we write or check the versions with you.
Will this stop customers from emailing me?
It should cut down the common where is my order questions. We cannot promise to remove them all, but clear updates normally leave much less for customers to ask.

desc:
Order status and tracking notification setup gives customers news about their parcel without having to ask. Ecom Swift LLC writes and tests your confirmation, shipped, delivered and delay messages, and adds a tracking page if you want one.

## What are order status updates?

Order status updates are the automatic messages a customer receives as an order moves: confirmation after payment, a shipped notice with tracking, a delivery message and a note when something is late. They can arrive by email, text message or on a tracking page.

Most stores have basic versions of these messages from day one, in the default wording. The defaults work, but they often feel generic, miss details and sometimes carry a broken tracking link.

## Why customers write when they hear nothing

Most where-is-my-order emails are not really complaints. They are requests for news. A shopper who has paid and heard nothing begins to wonder if the order was lost. Each of those emails takes your time to answer, and the same answer could have been sent automatically.

Good messages replace the worry with information. They say what has happened, what happens next and where to look for details.

## How clear messages change the customer experience

Status messages are some of the most-read emails you send, because customers open them to find out about something they paid for. That makes them a good place to show your brand, set expectations and reduce support work.

A shipped email with a working tracking link answers the most common question in advance. A delay notice, sent early and honestly, keeps goodwill that silence would lose. A tracking page lets shoppers check progress themselves at any hour. We cannot promise that customers will stop writing, but fewer need to.

## What a complete status update set includes

- An order confirmation that repeats items, address and delivery choice.
- A shipped email with the carrier name and a tracking link that opens the right page.
- A delivered message, with a gentle prompt to contact you if something is wrong.
- A delay notice for orders that take longer than promised.
- Handling for partial shipments, so each parcel is explained.
- Email styling in your brand colors and tone.
- A tracking page on your store, with order lookup if needed.
- Optional text message updates for shipped and delivered stages.
- Order statuses that match how your team really works.
- A test of every message with a real order.

## What we do

We start by reading your current messages and your process, so we know what each status means in your store. We then rewrite the emails in your voice, apply your brand styling and check that the right details are filled in automatically.

Next, we test. We place orders, fulfil them with tracking and confirm that each message arrives with the right content and a working link. If you choose a tracking page or text updates, we build and test those the same way. For text messages, we set up the sending tool so that it only contacts people who have agreed to receive messages.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many messages we write, whether we add a tracking page and whether we include text updates and multi-order testing.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Name the carrier and give the tracking link in the shipped email.
- Say what happens next in every message.
- Keep wording short and friendly.
- Send a delay notice as soon as you know.
- Test messages on a phone before they go live.

**Avoid:**
- Using one vague message for every stage.
- Sending texts without clear permission.
- Burying the tracking link under a long block of text.
- Promising a delivery date the carrier does not support.
- Leaving old default wording in a few places.

## Who this is for

This suits a store whose inbox fills with where-is-my-order questions. It suits a brand that wants every customer touchpoint to feel consistent, including the email after purchase. It also suits an international seller whose parcels take longer and need more explanation.

## What we need from you

Send us your logo, brand colors, preferred tone and any messages you like today. We need collaborator or staff access to notification settings, and the details of your tracking or text tools. We do not need your password. We reply with draft messages for your approval before anything goes live.
